Ranges
rānj'ĕz
n. pl. (a set of ranks or rows; a stand for cooking pots; in Kings, the ordered ranks of the temple guard)
Old French range, a row or rank. The Authorized Version uses it for two different Hebrew words: a cooking stand, and the drawn-up ranks of armed men.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The word first appears in the purity law: whatever a dead creeping thing falls upon is unclean, “whether it be oven, or ranges for pots, they shall be broken down: for they are unclean” (Lev 11:35) — the household fixtures themselves were to be demolished, not merely scoured. Then it names the ranks of the guard at the crowning of Joash. Athaliah had destroyed all the seed royal; one infant had been hidden six years in the house of God; and Jehoiada armed the captains and set them about the boy king: “ye shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand: and he that cometh within the ranges, let him be slain: and be ye with the king as he goeth out and as he cometh in” (2Ki 11:8). When Athaliah came crying Treason, treason, the priest commanded, “Have her forth without the ranges: and him that followeth her kill with the sword. For the priest had said, Let her not be slain in the house of the LORD” (2Ki 11:15). Two details in that order deserve notice: the ranks were drawn to protect a child, and the house of the LORD was not to be defiled with blood even in the execution of a murderess.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a range as a row; a rank; things in a line; also a kitchen grate, and the extent or compass of a thing.

expand to see more

RANGE, n. A row; a rank; things in a line; as a range of buildings; a range of mountains.

2. A class; an order.

3. A kitchen grate; a stand or grate for pots.

Key Scripture

Lev 11:35 — "And every thing whereupon any part of their carcase falleth shall be unclean; whether it be oven, or ranges for pots, they shall be broken down: for they are unclean, and shall be unclean unto you."

2Ki 11:8 — "And ye shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand: and he that cometh within the ranges, let him be slain: and be ye with the king as he goeth out and as he cometh in."

2Ki 11:15 — "But Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of the hundreds, the officers of the host, and said unto them, Have her forth without the ranges: and him that followeth her kill with the sword. For the priest had said, Let her not be slain in the house of the LORD."

Modern Corruption

The preservation of the messianic line ran, at one point, through a hidden infant and a ring of armed men, and Scripture treats the protection of the vulnerable as an ordered duty rather than a sentiment.

expand to see more

Second Kings 11 is one of the narrowest passes in redemptive history. Athaliah, daughter of Ahab, seized the throne of Judah and destroyed all the seed royal — a systematic massacre of the house of David, the line to which the covenant of 2 Samuel 7 was attached. One infant was stolen away by Jehosheba and hidden with his nurse in a bedchamber, then six years in the house of God. The whole promise of a son of David to sit upon his throne for ever hung, humanly speaking, on a woman's courage and a locked room. When the boy was brought out, Jehoiada did not trust to acclamation: he armed the captains, gave them the spears and shields that had been King David's, set them in ranks about the child, and gave a standing order — he that cometh within the ranges, let him be slain. Protection was organised, armed, and specific. Two things are worth drawing from it. The first is that God's preservation of His promises regularly runs through ordinary human faithfulness at great personal risk, and Jehosheba's name is in the record. The second is the shape of the duty: the ranks were drawn around a child who could not defend himself. Psalm 82:3-4 puts it as a command — defend the poor and fatherless; deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew kiyrayim (H3600), a pair of cooking stands, ranges for pots; sederah (H7713), a rank or row, of the temple guard; bayith (H1004), the house, which was not to be defiled with blood.

expand to see more

Hebrew kiyrayim (H3600) — a stand or range for pots; used only in the purity law of Leviticus 11:35.

Hebrew sederah (H7713) — a rank, a row, an ordered line; the armed ranks about the boy king; 2 Kings 11:8, 11:15.

Hebrew qesher (H7195) — a conspiracy, treason; Athaliah's cry when she saw the king by a pillar as the manner was; 2 Kings 11:14.

Usage

"“Whether it be oven, or ranges for pots, they shall be broken down” — the fixtures themselves demolished."

"“He that cometh within the ranges, let him be slain” — a ring of armed men round a child."

"“Let her not be slain in the house of the LORD” — even a just execution kept outside the sanctuary."
